bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source snapshot / saved sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ of size 3 in `lex_multiline_string()` at `src/lib/lwan-config.c:345`. The harness copies the 32769-byte witness into `static_data[32768]`, truncating it to 32768 bytes, and `config_open_for_fuzzing()` then asks the project lexer to parse the first 32767 bytes of that copy. While `parse_key_value()` is lexing a value that begins with `"""`, `lex_multiline_string()` searches for a closing `"""` delimiter by evaluating `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` on each loop iteration. The vulnerable loop never checks that at least three bytes remain before `lexer->end`, so on the witnessed unterminated multiline string it reaches the tail of the configured span and still performs the 3-byte compare. That probe crosses one byte past `static_data`, matching the saved ASan stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value`. The staged fix adds `remaining(lexer) < 3` immediately before the `strncmp` call.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the copied fuzz buffer and its clipped length: the fuzz-only helper materializes the logical parser span as `len - 1` bytes of attacker-controlled data.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 32769 bytes. `src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc` clamps that to 32768 bytes, copies the prefix into `static_data`, and then calls this helper with `data = static_data` and `len = 32768`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The unchecked 3-byte terminator probe is issued from this call site after the multiline-string scan has reached the tail of the configured fuzz buffer.

root_cause.description: Missing bounds check before the 3-byte terminator probe. The vulnerable loop calls `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` without first proving that at least three bytes remain before `lexer->end`; the fix inserts `if (remaining(lexer) < 3) break;` immediately before this line.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness copies attacker-controlled bytes into the fixed global array that the project parser later scans, clipping the saved witness from 32769 bytes down to the first 32768 bytes.

parser_admitted.description: The parser has already accepted a key and `=` and is now pulling the value through `lex_next()`. On the witnessed path that call reaches `lex_config()` and selects `lex_multiline_string()` for an opening `"""` value.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness truncates the 32769-byte witness to 32768 bytes, copies that prefix into `static_data[32768]`, and hands the global buffer to `config_open_for_fuzzing()`.

The fuzz-only helper initializes the project lexer on the first 32767 bytes of the copied buffer, establishing `lexer.pos/start` at `static_data` and `lexer.end` at the tail of that logical parser span.
While a value is being lexed, the parser encounters an opening `"""`, switches into multiline-string scanning, and then advances toward EOF without finding a closing `"""` terminator.

At the tail of the configured span, `lex_multiline_string()` still executes `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` even though fewer than three bytes remain before `lexer.end`, and that 3-byte read crosses one byte past `static_data`.

fine_trace.note: The staged `poc` is 32769 bytes, so the harness clips it to `size = 32768` and copies only that prefix into the global `static_data[32768]` array before calling the project parser. Because the array is completely filled, no extra in-array terminator byte is appended.

Source. The fuzz-only helper consumes the copied buffer and its clipped length and asks the project lexer to parse only the first `len - 1` bytes. On the witnessed path that means `data = static_data` and the logical parser span is 32767 bytes long.

The lexer state is initialized over `[static_data, static_data + 32767)`, with `lexer.end` set to `static_data + 32767`. There is therefore only one copied slack byte left in `static_data` beyond the logical parser span, not enough room for an unchecked 3-byte terminator probe at the tail.

While `parse_key_value()` is requesting the value token, the lexer sees an opening `"""` delimiter and switches into multiline-string scanning. The saved witness contains many `"""` triples and no `'''` triples, so the crashing path is the double-quote form of `lex_multiline_string()`.

The multiline scanner materializes the closing delimiter as `end = "\"\"\""` and consumes the remaining two opening quotes. After `advance_n(2)`, `lexer->pos` and `lexer->start` point at the first content byte after the opening delimiter.

No earlier iteration finds the `"""` terminator, so the loop keeps advancing one byte at a time through the multiline contents. By the crashing iteration, the scan has reached the tail of the configured span and `lexer->pos` is on the last 0 or 1 parser bytes before `lexer.end`.

Root cause. The vulnerable loop performs the 3-byte terminator probe unconditionally; it never checks that `lexer->end - lexer->pos >= 3` before issuing `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)`. The staged fix adds `if (remaining(lexer) < 3) break;` immediately before this line.

Sink. On the witnessed tail state, `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` reads past the copied fuzz buffer. With only 0 or 1 parser bytes left and just one slack byte in `static_data`, the 3-byte probe reaches `static_data + 32768`, matching the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow` READ of size 3 at this call site.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The sink is the project call site at `lex_multiline_string` line 345, which is the first project frame immediately beneath ASan's interceptor `strncmp` frame.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value -> parser_next -> config_read_line` matches the fine trace's multiline-string admission, tail scan, and unchecked compare.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The clipped witness fills `static_data`, `config_open_for_fuzzing()` initializes a 32767-byte parser span over it, the parser then enters `lex_multiline_string()` on an opening `"""` value, and the unchecked 3-byte probe is finally executed at the tail.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_18562 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` `READ of size 3` in `lex_multiline_string` with stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value`.

format.name: raw lwan config byte stream
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 32769-byte blob in `gt_results/arvo_18562/poc`. Its verified trigger semantics are limited to the saved truncation and parser state: the harness copies only the first 32768 bytes into `static_data`, `config_open_for_fuzzing()` parses only the first 32767 bytes of that copy, and on the crashing path `parse_key_value()` encounters an opening `"""` value whose closing `"""` terminator is not found before that parser boundary. `lex_multiline_string()` therefore reaches the tail with fewer than three bytes left before `lexer->end` and still executes `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)`. The saved artifacts do not justify a broader input class beyond this witnessed clipped layout and unterminated multiline-string state.
